trial_court: Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Kadur, M.C. No.28/2013
case_name: Chaluvaraj vs Smt Girija H R @ Dhanalakshmi

parties.respondent_defendant: SMT GIRIJA H R @ DHANALAKSHMI, wife/respondent

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2003. The husband worked as a teacher, while the wife was a permanent teacher in a Government School. They had a son born in 2004. The husband claimed that his wife left him and never returned, seeking dissolution of marriage on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion means the intentional abandonment of the spouse by the other without consent and a reasonable cause.
legal_principles.held: The Apex court has held that desertion means the intentional abandonment of the spouse by the other without consent and a reasonable cause.
cited_cases: LACHMAN UTAMCHAND KIRIPALANI Vs. MENA @ MOTA, (1964) AIR SC 40
DEBANANDA TAMULI Vs. KAKUMONI KATAKY, (2022) SCC Online SC 187

legal_principles.principle: A deserted spouse must prove that there is a factum of separation and an intention on the part of the deserting spouse to bring cohabitation to a permanent end.
legal_principles.held: It has further been held that a deserted spouse must prove that there is a factum of separation and there is an intention on the part of deserting spouse to bring the cohabitation to a permanent end.
cited_cases: LACHMAN UTAMCHAND KIRIPALANI Vs. MENA @ MOTA, (1964) AIR SC 40
DEBANANDA TAMULI Vs. KAKUMONI KATAKY, (2022) SCC Online SC 187

outcome.final_order: The appeal filed by the husband under Section 13(1) (ia) (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage on grounds of cruelty and desertion is dismissed.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
divorce proceedings in Karnataka High Court
